title: Enterprise request orchestration playbook for hosted API multi-inputs (chat, streaming, toolcalls, structured)
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting feature requests that span chat+streaming+tool-calls+structured outputs. Current intake is ad-hoc across sales/support/SEs which causes slow onboarding, SLA mismatches, and surprise engineering effort. This ticket defines a canonical orchestration playbook to triage, enrich, and route enterprise-hosted-API feature requests into prioritized lanes.
goals: 1) Create a deterministic decision flow that maps inbound enterprise requests to priority lanes (SLA tier, product track, Dedicated vs Hosted, required compliance). 2) Reduce time-to-triage for enterprise requests to <48h. 3) Surface required preflight artifacts (security checklist, data residency, model/throughput estimates) to customers before engineering intake. 4) Provide clear routing rules to automation and CS/SEs so requests are consistently scored and scheduled.
scope: Includes: taxonomy for request types, enrichment checklist, SLA-based priority mapping, example routing rules, templated responses for SE/CS, dashboard signals for intake throughput. Excludes: backend enforcement in console (separate ENG ticket), changes to pricing model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical taxonomy (<= 12 categories) published in Confluence and linked from intake form.
- A runnable rubric that maps category + SLA tier + estimated QPS to priority bucket (P0/P1/P2) with examples.
- Intake form and CS/SE triage checklist drafted and validated with 3 SEs.
- Automation rules (pseudo-code) for routing to PM backlog or sales-engineer queue captured.
- Pilot with two enterprise customers completed and learnings documented.

ENG tickets ENG-19834 (preflight API) and ENG-20401 (validation rules) are dependencies. Keep implementation idempotent and return structured error codes for triage automation.

post_mortem_considerations: Capture any mismatches between automated score and human triage during pilot; log false positives where a request was auto-routed to lower priority. Feed these into a weekly tuning cycle for the rubric.
implementation_risks:
- Under-specified customer telemetry may cause many manual reviews.
- Over-aggressive automation could misroute high-impact but low-data requests.
- Dedicated routing opt-out may increase operational cost if misclassified.
